matching_policy: Source spans and graph_refs plus status yield review candidates only. Do not intersect gold requirement IDs with model-generated IDs. Human review establishes whether the explanation detects the intended defect.

source_requirements.statement: Read source_id from the request and FAST_KEY from the environment. Use fast.fetch first only when FAST_KEY is present; pass both source_id and FAST_KEY. If the first attempt fails transiently, retry exactly once. Never retry a non-transient first failure.
source_requirements.scope: input acquisition, preferred-tool selection and retry
clauses: Read both values from their specified origins.
Absent FAST_KEY skips fast.fetch and goes directly to archive.fetch.
The preferred call receives source_id and FAST_KEY.
Only a transient first failure permits one retry; no third fast attempt and no retry for a non-transient first failure.

source_refs.quote:
1. Read source_id from the user's request and read FAST_KEY from the environment.
2. If FAST_KEY is present, try fast.fetch first with source_id and FAST_KEY; if it is absent, go directly to archive.fetch without calling fast.fetch.
3. Retry fast.fetch exactly once only when its first attempt fails with a transient error; do not retry a non-transient first failure.

source_requirements.statement: Missing FAST_KEY, a non-transient first fast failure, or any failed retry leads to archive.fetch. Call archive.fetch at most once, with source_id as its only argument. On any fetch success, return that same successful response body unchanged and stop further fetch calls. On archive failure, return that error and stop without archive retry.
source_requirements.scope: fallback call, operand bindings and every return
clauses: Cover missing-key, non-transient-first-failure and failed-retry fallback paths.
Archive receives only source_id and is attempted at most once.
First-fast success returns first-fast body; retry success returns retry body; archive success returns archive body.
A successful return uses the same body unchanged and ends fetch calls.
Archive failure returns its own error and never retries archive.

source_refs.quote: 2. If FAST_KEY is present, try fast.fetch first with source_id and FAST_KEY; if it is absent, go directly to archive.fetch without calling fast.fetch.

4. After a non-transient first failure or any failed retry of fast.fetch, call archive.fetch with source_id.
5. Call archive.fetch at most once and pass source_id as its only argument.
6. On either tool's success, return that successful response's body value unchanged and make no further fetch calls.
7. If archive.fetch fails, stop and return its error; do not retry archive.fetch.

source_requirements.statement: Never pass FAST_KEY to archive.fetch or diagnostic output anywhere in the workflow.
source_requirements.scope: entire graph, including fallback and diagnostic operations
clauses: Exclude the FAST_KEY-produced result from archive inputs.
The prohibition applies to diagnostic output and all workflow paths, not just the preferred-tool block.
A declared prohibition is not proof of behavior hidden inside an open opcode.

source_requirements.statement: Before returning from every success or failure path, append the final status to local status.txt.
source_requirements.scope: every terminal path, before its return
clauses: Append status for first-fast success, retry success, archive success and archive failure.
The append precedes the corresponding return and targets local status.txt.
Literal status values success and failure are acceptable representations of final status; source does not demand propagating a full response object.
